name: Amphotericin B deoxycholate
executiveSummary: Conventional polyene. Usual adult/pediatric **0.5–1 mg/kg/day IV** (common max **50 mg/day**). High nephrotoxicity and infusion reactions — prefer lipid formulations when available.
indications:
## Indications

- Severe systemic mycoses (candida, cryptococcus, aspergillus, mucorales, etc.) when lipid alternatives are unavailable or by cost/availability.
- Leishmaniasis / other uses per protocol.

## Precautions

- Nephrotoxicity, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia — NS hydration, electrolyte replacement, creatinine monitoring.
- Infusion reactions (fever, chills): premedication per center; infuse slowly (2–6 h).
- **Do not confuse mg/kg with liposomal** (doses differ ~5×).

> Optional institutional test dose. Never bolus.

adulto.dose: Usual: **0.5–1 mg/kg/day IV** (common max **50–70 mg/day** per label/protocol). Escalation: start **0.25–0.5 mg/kg** and increase **0.2 mg/kg/day** to target, or institutional rapid scheme. Cryptococcal meningitis (classic induction): **0.7–1 mg/kg/day** ± flucytosine.
adulto.administration: Reconstitute with sterile water only; dilute in 5% dextrose (not NS — precipitates). Usual conc. ≤ 0.1 mg/mL; infuse **2–6 h** protected from light.
adulto.notes: Incompatible with NS and many Y-site drugs. Monitor K⁺, Mg²⁺, creatinine.

pediatrico.dose: Start **0.5 mg/kg/day**, increase **0.2 mg/kg/day** to **1 mg/kg/day** (max **50 mg/day**). Rapid scheme: start **0.25 mg/kg** per card. Severe: up to **1–1.5 mg/kg/day** under ID.
pediatrico.notes: Dose by weight. Same toxicity as adults.

neonatal.dose: Orientative: **0.5–1 mg/kg/day**; many NICUs prefer liposomal. Confirm protocol.

stability:
## Stability

- Dilution in 5% dextrose: per label (usually immediate use / hours light-protected).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Fever, chills, nausea, phlebitis, nephrotoxicity, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, anemia, hepatotoxicity.
